Consult Summary:
- 35-year-old female, 4 weeks post-C-section, presents with sudden onset shortness of breath and a recent cough; advised urgent hospital review due to suspicion of possible pulmonary embolism.
- Allergic to Ibuprofen and recent use of Codeine (now ceased); no other significant past medical history reported.

Problem List:

Issue 1:
- Acute onset shortness of breath for 1 hour while at rest (watching TV); never experienced before.
- Associated symptoms: recent onset cough (started yesterday), palpitations, chest soreness on deep inspiration and tenderness at C-section scar.
- No chest pain at rest, no hemoptysis, no production of sputum, no recent viral illness, no mention of leg symptoms.
- Systems review: denies chest pain except with deep inspiration, no fever, coughs and colds several months ago.
- Risk factor: recent C-section (4 weeks ago).
- Differential diagnosis: pulmonary embolism (discussed), less likely infection.
- No home monitoring data (heart rate, oxygen) except heart rate counted at 30 beats in unspecified time frame; heart "running slightly fast" per doctor.

Issue 2:
- Post C-section recovery (4 weeks post-op).
- C-section scar is reported as tender.
- Has been taking painkillers (Codeine), now stopped for approximately 1 week.

Issue 3:
- Ibuprofen allergy.
- Reaction details unspecified; patient unable to recall reaction specifics.

Medications:
- Codeine (dose/route/frequency not documented; last taken ~1 week ago).
- No ongoing regular medications currently reported.

Allergies:
- Ibuprofen (reaction details not specified).

Past Medical History:
- C-section 4 weeks ago.
- No other past medical problems reported.

Social History:
- Lives with baby; partner at work at the time of consult.
- No smoking history mentioned.
- No alcohol history mentioned.

Preventative History:
- No information on cervical screening, mammogram, prostate blood test, fecal occult blood test, bone mineral density, vaccinations, optometry review, or skin check.

Physical Examination:
- No formal physical exam performed.
- Heart rate self-counted (patient: 30 beats, but duration not specified); doctor interprets as "slightly fast."
- No vitals documented.

Plan:
- Advise urgent hospital attendance for assessment for possible pulmonary embolism.
- Do not take any further medications (including Codeine) until assessed.
- Take essential supplies for baby to hospital.
- No ambulance arranged; patient to self-transport.
- No follow-up arranged; immediate hospital review advised.

Quality checks:

●	Missing but clinically expected elements: 
   - Allergies: reaction to Ibuprofen not described.
   - No documentation of smoking, alcohol, or complete medication reconciliation.
   - Vitals (blood pressure, pulse oximetry, temperature, formal heart rate) not documented.
   - No documented physical exam findings beyond subjective description.
   - No preventative care or cancer screening information.
●	Internal conflicts: None identified.
●	Transcript quality: Clear, focused on acute presentation; no significant background noise or inaudible sections.
